title: Sensory Urbanism Proceedings 2008
article_description: A proceedings collection of 26+ theoretical essays and case studies on sensory urbanism, public space design, and embodied experience in urban environments. Chapters cover artist interventions, urban planning theory, temporary autonomous zones, and public space activism. No empirical studies or statistical analyses are included.
methodology: Qualitative narrative review and case study analysis. Includes theoretical frameworks from Situationist International, contemporary art theory, and urban planning discourse. No quantitative data collection or statistical testing.
limitations: Proceedings format: papers represent diverse, sometimes inconsistent theoretical frameworks
No experimental designs or control conditions
Limited peer review process typical of conference proceedings
Focus on European and Indian case studies; limited geographic generalization
overall_theory_links: Post-industrial urban renewal and adaptive reuse
extraction_notes: This document is a proceedings collection containing 26+ theoretical essays on sensory urbanism and public space design. It is NOT an empirical research article and contains NO statistical findings, experimental designs, or quantitative data analysis. The finding array is empty (0 findings) and the article is correctly classified as narrative_review. All chapters are qualitative theoretical contributions discussing design philosophy, case studies of urban interventions, and conceptual frameworks rather than empirical research with measurable outcomes.
